_about: Public-domain Harvey Newcomb (1803-1863), Congregational minister and writer for the young, for the Word Hoard: A Practical Directory for Young Christian Females, The Anabaptists, Protestants, Sabbath School Teacher's Aid, The Young Lady's Guide, The Closet, The Four Pillars, The False Prophet, How to be a Man, Christianity Demonstrated, A Cyclopedia of Missions, The Harvest and the Reapers, Kind Words for Children, and Anecdotes for Boys. Texts are from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 97 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

newcomb-young-females: A practical directory for young Christian females : being a series of letters from a brother to a younger sister (Boston : Massachusetts Sabbath School Society, 1833)
newcomb-anabaptists: The Anabaptists : being an account of the progress of the Reformation in Germany, from the Diet of Worms to the death of Frederic, Elector of Saxony (Boston : Massachusetts Sabbath School Society, 1836)
newcomb-protestants: Protestants: being a continuation of the Reformation in Germany from 1525 to 1532 (Boston, Massachusetts Sabbath School Society, 1839)
newcomb-young-lady: The young lady's guide to the harmonious development of Christian character ([n.p.], 1841)
newcomb-closet: The Closet: Being an Aid to Private Devotion ; Containing Directions and (J.B. Dow, 1841)
newcomb-four-pillars: The four pillars, or, The truth of Christianity demonstrated, in four distinct and independent series of proofs : together with an explanation of the types and prophecies concerning the Messiah (Boston : S. Goldsmith, and Crocker & Brewster, 1842)
newcomb-false-prophet: The false prophet; or, An account of the rise and progress of the Mohammedan religion: comprising the history of the church, from the close of the fifth to the beginning of the seventh century; together with a concise view of the prophecies relating to Mohammed and his followers (Boston, Massachusetts Sabbath school society, 1844)
newcomb-how-to-be-man: How to be a man : a book for boys, containing useful hints on the formation of character (Boston : Gould, Kendall, and Lincoln, 1847)
newcomb-christianity-demonstrated: Christianity demonstrated; in four distinct and independent series of proofs; with an explanation of the types and prophecies concerning the Messiah (Boston, Gould, Kendall and Lincoln, 1848)
newcomb-cyclopedia-missions: A cyclopedia of missions : containing a comprehensive view of missionary operations throughout the world : with geographical descriptions, and accounts of the social, moral, and religious condition of the people (New York : Scribner, 1855)
newcomb-harvest-reapers: The harvest and the reapers; homework for all, and how to do it (Boston, Gould and Lincoln; New York, Sheldon, Blakeman & co.; [etc., etc.], 1858)
newcomb-kind-words: Kind words for children to guide them in the path of peace ([n.p.], 1859)
